original_text: \citet{Wu2024} found that the turbulent torques dominate the evolution of the orbit once the mass ratio between the planet and the star falls below $\sim10^{-5}$
injected_text: \citet{Wu2024} found that the turbulent torques dominate the evolution of the orbit once the mass ratio between the planet and the star falls below $\sim10^{-4}$
rationale: Wu2024 reports the threshold mass ratio as ~10^{-5}; shifting it to ~10^{-4} moves the stated value by approximately one order of magnitude — a 1–2σ mis-quote of the specific quantitative threshold reported in that paper — while leaving the cite key, surrounding prose, and direction of the claim intact, so a careful reader comparing to Wu2024 flags the discrepancy but a casual reader does not.
ground_truth_description: The threshold mass ratio below which turbulent torques dominate was changed from ~10^{-5} (as reported in Wu2024) to ~10^{-4}, a mild but detectable quantitative mis-quote of the cited paper's result.

truth.claim_sentence_verbatim: \citet{Wu2024} found that the turbulent torques dominate the evolution of the orbit once the mass ratio between the planet and the star falls below $\sim10^{-5}$, which corresponds to the EMRI regime in the case of AGN disks.
truth.section_location: Sec. 2 (Inspiration for our turbulent torque model)

original_text: mass ratio $q=5\times10^{-5}$ in its final four-year evolution at redshift $z=0.276$
injected_text: mass ratio $q=5\times10^{-5}$ in its final four-year evolution at redshift $z=0.267$
rationale: Swapping adjacent digits 7↔6 in the redshift value in the abstract (0.276→0.267) while the body correctly states z=0.276 in Eq.(golden) and the Conclusion, triggering an abstract_vs_body_match predicate failure at major severity.
ground_truth_description: The redshift of the golden EMRI in the abstract was changed from z=0.276 to z=0.267 (digit swap of adjacent digits 7 and 6), while the correct value z=0.276 remains in the body (Results section Eq. golden and Conclusion).

truth.location_cue: mass ratio q=5times10^{-5} in its final four-year evolution at redshift z=0.267
truth.paired_location: Results section Eq. (golden) and Conclusion paragraph
truth.quantity_label: redshift z of the golden EMRI

rationale: Changing the exponent in the denominator from a^3 to a^4 alters the power-law dependence of the GW-driven inspiral rate on semi-major axis, producing an equation inconsistent with the Peters (1964) formula that Wolfram symbolic equality would refute against the correct a^{-3} dependence.
ground_truth_description: The denominator exponent of semi-major axis a in the GW-driven inspiral rate equation was changed from a^3 to a^4, corrupting the Peters formula for the rate of change of semi-major axis due to gravitational wave emission.

truth.equation_location: Sec. 3 (Model), second displayed equation for dot{a}_{GW}
truth.term_role: semi-major axis power-law factor in Peters inspiral rate formula

original_text: Hence, this work strongly motivates MHD simulations of gas disks embedded near-coalescence EMRIs to extract maximum science in the LISA era.
injected_text: Hence, this work strongly motivates MHD simulations of gas disks embedded near-coalescence EMRIs to extract maximum science in the LISA era, and further demonstrates that turbulence-driven stochastic torques will generically dominate orbital evolution across all classes of compact binary inspirals embedded in any astrophysical accretion disk, regardless of the mass ratio or turbulence source.
rationale: The added clause asserts that stochastic torques 'generically dominate' for all compact binary classes and all astrophysical disks, but the Results are confined to a single golden EMRI with q=5e-5 in one parametric regime, providing no support for this sweeping universal claim; the overreach is grammatically integrated into the existing concluding sentence making it read as an organic author flourish.
ground_truth_description: A sweeping generalisation clause was appended to the final sentence of the Conclusion, claiming turbulent torques dominate all compact binary inspirals in any accretion disk, far beyond what the paper's single-system results support.

truth.affected_span_verbatim: Hence, this work strongly motivates MHD simulations of gas disks embedded near-coalescence EMRIs to extract maximum science in the LISA era.
